description: We are Night Owls , 4 member team . We are interested in space exploration and creating something on lunar landing site navigator .
summary:
Luna Scout is an interactive tool for exploring lunar landing options, especially near the Moon’s south pole. Users can choose a site and mission date to compare sunlight, direct-to-Earth visibility, terrain slope, elevation, and surface roughness. A mission planner shows operational windows and ranks candidate regions against adjustable screening limits, while a spacecraft navigator lets users fly between sites and see changing illumination and Earth-link status.

The project combines a minimalist frontend with a Python backend that uses NASA/JPL SPICE geometry and lunar elevation data from LRO’s LOLA instrument. It makes complex mission-planning information easier for students, the public, and early-stage teams to explore. Its rankings are regional screening estimates, not certification that a spacecraft can land safely.
details:
Luna Scout is a web-based tool for screening landing sites at the Moon’s south pole. The user picks one of six reference sites or any custom coordinate, plus a date. Using NASA data, Luna Scout computes the real positions of the Sun and Earth, builds a terrain horizon from LRO/LOLA elevation data (up to 20 m resolution), and produces a mission timeline of sunlight, darkness, and Earth-visibility windows, with estimated solar energy. It also measures terrain slope and roughness, and ranks sites with editable safety gates and a transparent 0-100 score that explains each ranking. A survey of the whole 80°S-90°S cap (11,553 points) shortlists twelve candidates for detailed analysis. A 3D spacecraft flight simulator lets users fly around the Moon and land at a chosen site while seeing live lighting and Earth-visibility status. Results export as CSV and JSON.

Benefits

It brings terrain, lighting, and Earth-visibility analysis together in one tool instead of several separate ones. Its scoring is transparent and editable, it states its limits honestly, and it runs locally with bundled data, so results are reproducible. The simulator makes complex lunar geometry easy to understand.

Intended impact

To help planners, students, and researchers quickly shortlist and compare candidate landing regions, and to help the public understand why the lunar south pole is both valuable and difficult. It is an educational screening prototype, not a landing-safety certification.

Tools used

Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS; FastAPI, NumPy, SpiceyPy, Rasterio, PyProj; Three.js (WebGL); pytest and Node.js tests. NASA data: LRO/LOLA elevation models, NAIF/JPL SPICE kernels, and NASA/GSFC/ASU LROC imagery. Developed on standard laptops, with no special hardware.

Creativity

It combines scientific analysis with an interactive flight experience. It models the full Sun and Earth disks, including partial visibility at sunrise and sunset. It uses a two-stage approach, a fast polar-cap survey followed by detailed analysis of a shortlist. Its ranking works as an explainable “what-if” tool rather than a black box.

Factors considered

Scientific accuracy (correct lunar frames, curvature, parallax, elevation scaling); safety metrics (slope, roughness, lighting, Earth visibility) without assuming higher ground is safer; communications treated as geometric screening only; documented data resolution limits; reproducibility through checksums and exports; and clear, honest communication of uncertainty for non-expert users.
